legenda: Jetty of 1871: 6,700 ft (more than a mile). Bar: 10 ft in 1881, 11 ft in 1888, at low tide.
texto_para_tela: MORE THAN A MILE · 10 FT (1881) · 11 FT (1888)
nota: Os 6.700 pés são o comprimento do projeto de 1871 (Meyler, 1899, reproduzindo-o), não uma medição da obra pronta.
narracao: It was a jetty, a wall of timber and rock more than a mile long, from Rattlesnake Island to Deadman's Island. It closed the shallows between the islands, so the ebb tide, the water draining out of the estuary, had one channel left. Squeezed into one channel, it dug. By 1881, the bar had ten feet at low tide. By 1888, eleven.
